title: Calendar Reasoning: Odd Days and Weekday Puzzles

questions.question: An ordinary year has how many odd days?
questions.rationale: 365 = 52 weeks + 1 day. That single leftover day - the 'odd day' - is what shifts the weekday of a given date from one year to the next. A leap year leaves 2.

questions.question: Which of the following years is NOT a leap year?
questions.rationale: The Gregorian exception: divisible by 100 is NOT leap unless also divisible by 400. 1900 fails the 400 test (2000 passes). Exam papers love this century trap.

questions.question: The number of odd days in 300 consecutive years is:
questions.rationale: Each 100-year block (say 1601-1700) contains 24 leap years - the century year itself fails the 400 rule - so odd days = 24x2 + 76x1 = 124 -> 5. Stacking three centuries: 5+5+5 = 15 -> 1. The ladder to memorise: 100y = 5, 200y = 3, 300y = 1, 400y = 0.

questions.question: What day of the week was 15 August 1947?
26 January 1950, the day India became a Republic, was a:
If 1 January 2006 was a Sunday, then 1 January 2010 was a:
questions.rationale: Add odd days for 2006-2009: 1+1+2+1 = 5. Sunday + 5 = Friday. Only 2008 was leap, contributing the extra odd day.

questions.question: Which year will have the same calendar as 2023 (an ordinary year that began on a Sunday)?
questions.rationale: Running odd days from 2023: 2024(+2)=2, 2025(+1)=3, 2026(+1)=4, 2027(+1)=5, 2028(+2)=7 = 0. So 1 January 2029 falls on a Sunday, and 2029 is an ordinary year like 2023 - both repeat conditions met. 2028 is leap and starts on Saturday, so it cannot match; 2030 starts on Tuesday.

questions.question: In an ordinary (non-leap) year, which pair of months starts on the same weekday?
questions.rationale: In an ordinary year the same-weekday pairs are January & October, February/March & November, April & July, September & December. January-April and February-August are the LEAP-year pairings.

questions.question: A year repeats its calendar every 400 years because:
options: 400 years contain a whole number of weeks (zero odd days)
the leap cycle is exactly 4 years
questions.rationale: 400 years = 400x365 + 97 leap days = 146097 days = 20871 exact weeks, remainder 0. With 97 (not 100) leaps because 1700/1800/1900-type centuries fail the 400 rule - hence the exact repetition.

questions.question: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be 100 days later?
questions.rationale: 100 mod 7 = 2 (98 is 14 full weeks). Wednesday + 2 = Friday. Any 'N days later' question is just N mod 7 added to the weekday number.
